diagnostics.message: :module.forge_trust_validator_lambda: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.forge_trust_validator_lambda: explicit depends_on of :module.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references
The module already references the log group's name through logging_log_group, so its explicit dependency on the log group duplicates an implicit dependency.
The event target references the module's lambda_function_arn, already establishing its dependency on the module.
The permission already depends on the event rule through source_arn, and that rule explicitly depends on the Lambda module. Its direct depends_on on the module duplicates this transitive ordering.

The trust-policy update inserts the Lambda execution role as an AWS principal using a constructed ARN, but has no dependency on the module that creates that role. IAM validates role principals when updating trust policies, so this command can fail with an invalid principal if it runs before the module creates the role. Order the trust update after the Lambda module.
